question: How did Christianity spread so fast?

answers.label: It reached every city, class and region within a few generations
Through ordinary lives and care for the needy
Through the witness of the martyrs

overview.text: By about 112 a Roman governor found Christians of every age, rank and sex in cities and villages, and temples emptying. By about 200 Tertullian could claim they filled everything but the temples.
Christians spread through ordinary life in every city and through their care for the poor, orphans, the old and prisoners. Persecution itself drew attention: "the blood of Christians is seed".

The writers also name the mechanism: traveling evangelists. Origen says Christians made it their work to go round cities, villages and farms to win others, and Eusebius says the generation after the apostles sowed the word across the whole inhabited world.

quotes.author: Pliny the Younger (Roman governor)
quotes.english: Many of every age, every rank, and both sexes are and will be brought into danger. The contagion of this superstition has spread not only through the cities but through villages and farms too. ... It is certain that temples almost deserted have begun to be frequented again.
quotes.original: Multi enim omnis aetatis, omnis ordinis, utriusque sexus etiam vocantur in periculum et vocabuntur. Neque civitates tantum, sed vicos etiam atque agros superstitionis istius contagio pervagata est ... Certe satis constat prope iam desolata templa coepisse celebrari
quotes.context: A hostile witness from Bithynia, eighty years after the crucifixion.

quotes.author: Tertullian
quotes.english: We are of yesterday, and we have filled everything you have: cities, islands, forts, towns, market places, the very camps, tribes, town councils, the palace, the senate, the forum. We have left you only the temples.
quotes.original: Hesterni sumus, et vestra omnia implevimus, urbes insulas castella municipia conciliabula castra ipsa tribus decurias palatium senatum forum; sola vobis reliquimus templa.
quotes.context: Rhetoric, but meant to be believed by Roman readers.

quotes.author: Letter to Diognetus
quotes.english: Christians are not distinguished from other people by country, language or customs. They do not live in cities of their own, speak a strange dialect, or follow an odd way of life. ... They live in Greek and barbarian cities, as each one's lot was cast, and follow local customs in dress, food and the rest of life, yet they show a wonderful and admittedly strange way of life. They live in their own countries, but as foreigners.
quotes.original: Χριστιανοὶ γὰρ οὔτε γῇ οὔτε φωνῇ οὔτε ἔθεσι διακεκριμένοι τῶν λοιπῶν εἰσιν ἀνθρώπων. οὔτε γάρ που πόλεις ἰδίας κατοικοῦσιν οὔτε διαλέκτῳ τινὶ παρηλλαγμένῃ χρῶνται οὔτε βίον παράσημον ἀσκοῦσιν. ... κατοικοῦντες δὲ πόλεις ἑλληνίδας τε καὶ βαρβάρους, ὡς ἕκαστος ἐκληρώθη, καὶ τοῖς ἐγχωρίοις ἔθεσιν ἀκολουθοῦντες ἔν τε ἐσθῆτι καὶ διαίτῃ καὶ τῷ λοιπῷ βίῳ θαυμαστὴν καὶ ὁμολογουμένως παράδοξον ἐνδείκνυνται τὴν κατάστασιν τῆς ἑαυτῶν πολιτείας. πατρίδας οἰκοῦσιν ἰδίας, ἀλλ’
quotes.context: The new faith spread through ordinary lives in every city.

quotes.author: Tertullian
quotes.english: It is spent ... to feed and bury the poor, for boys and girls without means or parents, for the old confined at home, for the shipwrecked, and for any in the mines, on the islands or in prison for the cause of God. ... "See," they say, "how they love one another."
quotes.original: sed egenis alendis humandisque et pueris ac puellis re ac parentibus destitutis iamque domesticis senibus, item naufragis et si qui in metallis et si qui in insulis vel in custodiis, dumtaxat ex causa dei sectae
quotes.context: Pagan observers noticed Christian care for outsiders too. Emperor Julian complained that the "Galileans" fed pagan poor as well as their own.

quotes.author: Tertullian
quotes.english: Yet none of your more refined cruelty does any good; it is rather an attraction to the sect. We grow more numerous every time you mow us down: the blood of Christians is seed.
quotes.original: Nec quicquam tamen proficit exquisitior quaeque crudelitas vestra; illecebra est magis sectae. Plures efficimur, quotiens metimur a vobis: semen est sanguis Christianorum.

quotes.author: Origen of Alexandria
quotes.english: It is clear from this: Christians, so far as it lies with them, do not fail to sow the word everywhere in the inhabited world. Some, at least, have made it their work to go round not only cities but also villages and country estates, in order to make others too devout toward God.
quotes.original: δῆλον ἐκ τοῦ τὸ ὅσον ἐφ᾿ ἑαυτοῖς Χριστιανοὺς μὴ ἀμελεῖν τοῦ πανταχοῦ τῆς οἰκουμένης ἐπισπείρειν τὸν λόγον, τινὲς γοῦν ἔργον πεποίηνται ἐκπεριέρχεσθαι οὐ μόνον πόλεις ἀλλὰ καὶ κώμας καὶ ἐπαύλεις, ἵνα καὶ ἄλλους εὐσεβεῖς τῷ θεῷ κατασκευάσωσι.
quotes.context: Origen is answering Celsus, who had claimed Christians would not want everyone to become Christian. He adds that these traveling teachers sometimes refuse even food, and take only what they strictly need.

source.edition: Koetschau, GCS 2 (1899), working Greek in the library

quotes.author: Eusebius of Caesarea
quotes.english: These distinguished disciples built on the foundations of the churches that the apostles had laid in every place, increasing the preaching and sowing the saving seeds of the kingdom of heaven in breadth across the whole inhabited world. ... distributing their possessions to the needy; then, setting out on journeys abroad, they did the work of evangelists, eager to preach Christ to those who had never yet heard the word of faith, and to hand over the writing of the divine Gospels.
quotes.original: οἳ καὶ, ἅτε τηλικῶνδε ὄντες διαπρεπεῖς μαθηταὶ, τοὺς κατὰ πάντα τόπον τῶν ἐκκλησιῶν προκαταβληθέντας ὑπὸ τῶν ἀποστόλων θεμελίους ἐπῳκοδόμουν, αὔξοντες εἰς πλέον τὸ κήρυγμα καὶ τὰ σωτήρια σπέρματα τῆς τῶν οὐρανῶν βασιλείας ἀνὰ πᾶσαν εἰς πλάτος ἐπισπείροντες τὴν οἰκουμένην. ... ἐνδεέσι νέμοντες τὰς οὐσίας, ἔπειτα δὲ ἀποδημίας στελλόμενοι ἔργον ἐπετέλουν εὐαγγελιστῶν, τοῖς ἔτι πάμπαν ἀνηκόοις τοῦ τῆς πίστεως λόγου κηρύττειν τὸν Χριστὸν φιλοτιμούμενοι καὶ τὴν τῶν θείων εὐαγγελίων παραδιδόναι γραφήν.
quotes.context: Eusebius describes the generation after the apostles. The evangelists first gave their own property away, then traveled; he goes on to credit the power of the Spirit still working wonders through them, with crowds converted at a first hearing.

quotes.author: Julian the Apostate
quotes.english: Why do we not notice that their benevolence to strangers, their care for the graves of the dead and the pretended holiness of their lives have most increased atheism? ... The impious Galileans feed, besides their own, ours as well.
quotes.original: οὐδὲ ἀποβλέπομεν, ὡς μάλιστα τὴν ἀθεότητα συνηύξησεν ἡ περὶ τοὺς ξένους φιλανθρωπία καὶ ἡ περὶ τὰς ταφὰς τῶν νεκρῶν προμήθεια καὶ ἡ πεπλασμένη σεμνότης κατὰ τὸν βίον ... τρέφουσι δὲ οἱ δυσσεβεῖς Γαλιλαῖοι πρὸς τοῖς ἑαυτῶν καὶ τοὺς ἡμετέρους
quotes.context: Julian is the pagan emperor trying to build a pagan rival to Christian charity. In this official letter to his high priest of Galatia he concedes why the Galileans were winning converts, and his word for Christianity in the letter is atheism.

method: Every early quote was read in its Greek or Latin and translated for this page by Claude (Opus 5.5) on 13 October 2026. Each line names the printed edition it was read from.
